short: The prolonged allied siege that resulted in the fall of Sweden's last major stronghold in Swedish Pomerania.
full:
The Siege of Stralsund culminated in the capitulation of the city on 24 December 1715. Stralsund had been blockaded and intermittently attacked since 1711, but the final, intensive siege began in July 1715. An allied coalition of Prussian, Saxon, and Danish forces invested the city, which was defended in person by Charles XII after his return from exile in the Ottoman Empire.

Despite fierce resistance led by the Swedish king, the superior allied numbers and artillery eventually breached the defenses. Charles XII narrowly escaped across the Baltic Sea to Sweden just days before the garrison surrendered, marking the effective end of Sweden's presence in northern Germany.
